formal_statement: Under controlled empirical attack-score replay into chronological Edge-IIoTset telemetry, the Adaptive Asymptotic Trust Ceiling with Borderline Authorization Debt (AATC-BAD) will reduce cumulative malicious access (M_cum) under Cycle A (1:10 schedule) by at least 20% relative to Baseline B0 (from M_cum = 8.5 to M_cum <= 6.5) by demoting cyclic attack pulses to VERIFY policy, while maintaining uncompromised benign device ALLOW availability above 70% and false BLOCK rate below 1.0% on the untouched chronological evaluation stream.

testable_predictions.prediction_1_security: Cycle A cumulative access M_cum will decrease from 8.5 to <= 6.5 due to ceiling attenuation below T_allow = 0.80.
testable_predictions.prediction_2_availability: On the untouched 7,459-row chronological benign evaluation stream, ALLOW rate will remain >= 70.0% and BLOCK rate will remain <= 1.0%.
testable_predictions.prediction_3_recovery: Legitimate devices experiencing isolated overt false alarms will recover to ALLOW within 10 steps once debt clears.

falsification_criteria.falsified_if_no_security_gain: If Cycle A M_cum remains >= 8.0 (meaning the ceiling failed to prevent ALLOW access during attack pulses).
falsification_criteria.falsified_if_availability_collapses: If benign ALLOW rate drops below 70.0% or false BLOCK rate exceeds 2.0% on the untouched evaluation stream.
